items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I recorded with Buck and his band the 23rd of November, 1949... one featured Buck and I on a number we called B.C. and B.C.

ctx.x: It was in December 1943 that I made records with the great Lester Young. I had first met him when I was on tour with the Ralph Cooper orchestra in 1932 in Denver, Colorado. We were playing a theatre, and after finishing that, there was a dance. After the dance, the musicians came to the place where we were living which was known as a popular musicians hangout. The band that had played for the dance was the Blue Devils, with whom Lester Young was playing saxophone. We started a jam session, and that was when I…

When I came back from Europe, I met Lester again when he was playing with the Basie band. We got to talking. Then later on after he left Basie and had his own group, he came to play the Apollo Theatre with his group, while we were playing the show, and we renewed our acquaintance once again. It was shortly after this that the chance to record came up. I never knew exactly how it came about. Possibly, Buck Clayton, was not available.

I remember that the session was very informal, more of a happy get-together. There was no system for working things out. We all decided that if something was good and could be of use, and did it that way. Of course, he was featured more than anyone else, as this was supposed to be his group.

items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: And I was playing with Bill Coleman and I'd make that trip almost every week from Paris.

ctx.x: Switzerland has got the Alps and I used to go play in the Chikita Club in Bern, especially in the winter. And you could just see thousands of people going on up the mountains and everybody's got skis.

Young kids. Special trains to take you up there. And I was playing with Bill Coleman and I'd make that trip almost every week from Paris. I'd leave on Friday night and come back Monday. And during the week I'd play at the Blue Note with Lil Armstrong, Kansas Fields, Don Byas,
we were all in together. Played there for a long time. I played in, oh this was after, later, no in '49 when we came back after being there. I stayed nine months. Bishop never came back.
